The PKGBUILD defines standard sources, including configuration files, documentation, licenses, and prebuilt binary releases for aarch64 and x86_64 architectures, all fetched from the project's official GitHub repository. The `source` array entries use direct HTTPS URLs to GitHub's `raw` and `releases` endpoints, which is normal and expected for AUR packages. The checksums are provided for all sources, including architecture-specific binaries, so there is no reliance on 'SKIP' — enhancing trust in the integrity of the downloaded files.

During the sourcing of the PKGBUILD (as part of `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`), only top-level variable assignments and the implicit `pkgver()` function (not defined here, so defaults to the static `pkgver=4.9.0`) are evaluated. There is no `pkgver()` function present, so no command substitution or external downloads occur at parse time. All `source` URLs are constructed using static variables and do not involve dynamic or obfuscated fetching logic. No code execution, data exfiltration, or unsafe operations occur during this phase.

Thus, simply sourcing this PKGBUILD and downloading the sources as defined poses no security risk.
</details>
